unsettled: Currency of the National List: the list read is dated May 2017. The newest EFDA texts could not be read: Narcotic and Psychotropic Medicine Control Directive No. 1121/2025 (December 2025), whose text layer ends mid-word in Art. 26(2), so its later articles and any annexes (Art. 22(1)(l) refers to an 'Annex 1') are unread; and the 'New NPS Directive' file posted in September 2026, which has no machine-readable text. A news article, not used as a source of fact, mentions a national list released in 2024; it was not found on the EFDA site. Items absent from the 2017 list (for example ketamine, esketamine, tapentadol, buprenorphine) may be on a newer list, so every 'Not found' record is draft. The editor could save the full PDFs of Directive No. 1121/2025 and of the 'New NPS Directive' so that a reader can check them.

Coverage by reference: Proclamation No. 1112/2019 Art. 2(11) and (12) define narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances as those subject to control under the UN conventions ratified by Ethiopia, plus any the executive organ (EFDA) categorizes. The English text says only 'the Convention' (no separate definition); the Amharic names the narcotic drugs convention and the psychotropic substances convention. No date or schedule is fixed, and there is no 'as amended' wording; whether substances scheduled internationally after 28 February 2019 are covered was not decided, and the UN scheduling dates were not read. This affects every 'Covered by reference' record. The editor may also prefer to show only named listings and drop these records.

Art. 2(11) defines narcotic drugs as 'a medicine' (Amharic መድኃኒት) subject to control, and Art. 2(9) defines medicine by its use in diagnosis, treatment or prevention. Whether the definition reaches 1961-Convention drugs that are not used as medicines (heroin, cannabis, coca leaf and the fentanyl analogues, for example) is a question of interpretation. Art. 2(12) says 'any substance' (Amharic ንጥረ-ነገር), so the question does not arise for 1971-Convention items.

Methylphenidate and dexamfetamine are named only among the 19 names pre-printed in the National List's import-statistics form for psychotropic substances (Annex 2, form NPS/01/B), not in Part I, which prints only Schedules III and IV although the Purpose says Part 1 covers 'Schedules I – IV'. Decide whether the form counts as listing. Dexamfetamine is matched from the form's 'Dextroamphetamine' by name.
Tramadol: its national categorization comes from an undated EFDA notice (attachment filed under /2022/10/), which says it was included in the 'NPS List'. No list showing tramadol was found.

Proclamation No. 1112/2019: in both government copies read (fjli.gov.et and efda.gov.et), the text layer ends in Art. 11, so later provisions (any on lists, repeal and transition) were not read. Only the definitions in Art. 2 were used.
